subject: Capacity validation: dedicated pool expansion — load run results & sign-off
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@datauno.com>, DataUno Procurement <procurement@datauno.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity validation: dedicated pool expansion — load test plan & kickoff

Hi Samira / DataUno procurement team,

Per our renewal, we added an 8-GPU reserved pool (A10x8) for your production tenant and applied the throughput guarantees from the amended SOW: a guaranteed baseline of 280 tokens/sec sustained with an autoscale headroom up to 420 tokens/sec for short bursts. Before we close the loop on billing/term changes, we need DataUno to validate the expansion with a smoke + load run and sign off.

Attached: capacity-test-plan.pdf (test schedule, traffic profile, pass/fail criteria). High-level plan:
- Smoke: 10 min verify connectivity, KV cache warmup, prefix caching behavior
- Load: 30 min steady-state at target throughput (300 tokens/sec)
- Burst: 10x short bursts (1 min) to validate autoscale fallback and throttling

Pass criteria (from SOW):
- Sustained throughput >= 280 tokens/sec for 30 minutes
- p95 latency < 250 ms for inference responses at 1024 token context
- No more than 2 error-rate spikes >1% during the run

Proposed test window: Thu, Apr 30, 14:00–15:00 PDT. Please confirm attendees, and whether you'd like Redwood to run the test or if your SREs will execute the client-side driver.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
---

1) Can you confirm the network egress policy and whether the reserved pool is in our VPC or managed by Redwood? (We need this for our security checklist.)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@datauno.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2026 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Load run completed — high level results (attached: load-results-20260501.csv, grafana-load-screenshots.png)

Samira / team,

We completed the test window as scheduled. Summary: PASS against SOW pass/fail criteria. Details below; see attached CSV for the full time series and Grafana screenshots.

Run summary (steady-state 30 min target = 300 tokens/sec):
- Sustained throughput observed: 312 tokens/sec (30-min mean)
- p95 latency: 185 ms
- p99 latency: 420 ms (brief cold-cache spike at t+04:32)
- Error rate: 0.4% (transient 1.1% spike during initial KV cache warm-up, cleared by t+06:00)
- Autoscale behavior: Ramp to burst cap observed for 3/3 scheduled bursts; no failed fallbacks
- GPU utilization (per-A10): average 62% during steady-state, peaks 88% during bursts

Notes:
- The KV cache warm-up contributed to the p99 spike early in the run. We recommend one short warm-up cycle before your production traffic ramp to minimize user-facing tail latency.
- We traced two requests that hit a slow I/O path in your client-side driver; a short retry/timeout adjustment will eliminate those transient errors.

Next steps:
1) Dev will drop the monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds into your shared folder (monitoring-config.yaml attached)
2) Marissa / Sales to confirm the one-time renewal credit discussed and close the SOW amendment
3) DataUno to provide formal sign-off via DocuSign (we'll link the doc once Marissa confirms)

If you want a replay session, we can run through the Grafana dashboards and the CSV with your SREs.

Best,
Karthik
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@datauno.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Observations & monitoring config after load run

Hi Samira — quick technical notes from the run and the monitoring bundle I dropped in the shared Drive: monitoring-config.yaml attached.

Observations:
- KV cache warm-up (first 6 minutes) increases p99 by ~200–350 ms; recommended pre-warm = 3x short requests at ramp start.
- Autoscale latency cutoff: we observed the autoscaler hit burst capacity within 18s on average; cool-down back to baseline ~4m.
- Suggested alerts to add: p95_lat > 250ms sustained 3m, error_rate > 1% over 2m, GPU_mem_pressure > 90% 2m.

Monitoring bundle includes:
- Grafana dashboard JSON (links in Drive)
- Prometheus scrape config snippets for your agent-runner
- Alerting thresholds and recommended runbooks

I'll be available Tue morning if you want to walk the runbooks.

- Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
